name: save3ds_fuse
why: Mounts and rewrites Nintendo 3DS save and extdata formats as a filesystem, a good door into console storage internals.

brief.what_it_is: Save3DS is a Rust project for reading and writing Nintendo 3DS save data, extdata, and title databases. It has two parts: the library libsave3ds, and the save3ds_fuse program, which extracts, imports, or mounts an archive through FUSE. Inputs are 3DS storage (NAND, SD, cartridge, or a standalone save file) plus console-specific keys and dumps such as boot9.bin, otp.bin, and movable.sed. Outputs are a browsable and editable directory tree on the host, or an extracted or re-imported archive.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no explicit motivation. It describes the project as an 'Extract, import and FUSE program for common save format for 3DS'.
brief.how_it_works: save3ds_fuse takes an archive selector (such as --sdsave, --nandsave, --db, or --cart), a mount path, and a mode. The default mode mounts the archive as a virtual filesystem, and unmounting writes the changes back. --extract and --import move content between the archive and a host directory, and --touch opens and closes the archive to check that the resources are correct. Format parameters are passed through --format and follow the fs:USER service functions on the 3DS.

brief.install_notes: Unix-like systems need pkg-config and the FUSE library. The README lists Debian (libfuse-dev, pkg-config), CentOS (fuse-devel, pkgconfig), macOS (macfuse cask), and FreeBSD (fusefs-libs, pkgconf). For --no-default-features or Windows, FUSE is not needed. Beyond the build, you need dumps from your own 3DS: boot9.bin for almost every archive type, otp.bin for nandtitle, nandimport, and ticket databases, movable.sed for SD-related archives when --nand is not given, and for cartridge saves a CCI game dump, a private header, and AES key material (slot 0x2F, 0x19, and 0x1A keys as a file or hex). An optional performance tip is to pass -C target-feature=+aes to enable hardware AES.
brief.standout: It treats 3DS storage as an ordinary filesystem: a mount you can browse in a file manager, with saves written back on unmount. It covers NAND, SD, cartridge, and standalone save formats and title databases in one tool, and it documents hardware quirks found by experiment (broken last block in title databases, the extdata resize workaround).
brief.status: unknown. The fetched README describes a full feature set but shows no release version, date, or commit history. I did not fetch the repository's release or commit pages, so I cannot confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: FUSE mount mode is not available on Windows. Modifying a standalone --bare save invalidates its signature, so other tools are needed to fix it. NAND must be an unpacked cleartext filesystem, not a raw FAT image; the README points to ninfs for that layer. Extdata resizing is slow and can produce zero-size files that the 3DS cannot open, so the README recommends --import instead of mount mode for extdata. Extdata also needs /boss, /user, and /icon created by hand. Title database --format is not supported. Names longer than 16 bytes are rejected. The README warns that Windows-specific reserved names are not handled and may crash or error out. Card1 wear leveling is not fully understood. Quota.dat handling for NAND extdata is probably incomplete. The README says to back up your data before writing, and it requires console dumps you must produce yourself.
quotes: Extract, import and FUSE program for common save format for 3DS, written in rust.
Note that the supported NAND format is in unpacked cleartext filesystem.
Because of all the mess, it is recommended to use `--import` mode instead of mount mode if you intend to modify the content of an extdata.
Please always backup your data if you don't set this flag!
